text.p: Quaker Oats Co., which sold its unprofitable Snapple beverage business in May, Thursday reported stronger-than-expected second quarter earnings.
The food and beverage company reported second quarter profit of $75.8 million, or 57 cents a share, up from $64.6 million, or 47 cents a share, a year earlier.
Excluding a $10.6 million pretax loss on the sale of Snapple and pretax restructuring charges of $11.8 million, Quaker earned 65 cents a share, up 38 percent from a year ago.
That beat the consensus of analysts' estimates of 55 cents a share, according to Wall Street consultants First Call.
"Overall, we're very pleased with this quarter," Chairman William Smithburg said in a conference call.
"I think this shows that Quaker is turning around after a long ordeal with Snapple," said Goldman Sachs analyst Nomi Ghez.
She added that Quaker is showing the benefits of cost-cutting measures and an improved business mix.

One of the highlights of the second quarter for Quaker was a 39 percent volume increase for its ready-to-eat cereals. That included a 25 percent rise for boxed cereals such as Cap'n Crunch and Life, and value-priced Quaker bagged cereals up more than 90 percent.
"We're not going to be able to match that 39 percent going forward," Douglas Mills, Quaker Oats executive vice president in charge of the food businesses.
But he said Quaker remains "encouraged" by the prospects for all its cereals.
Mills declined to say specifically if Quaker's bagged cereal business is profitable. "We are happy with the financial structure of our bagged cereal business," he added.

Total food operating income in the quarter was $68.8 million after the pretax restructuring charge of $10.7 million for the consolidation of Brazilian pasta manufacturing operations. Excluding the charge, total foods profit was $79.5 million, up from $70.8 million a year ago.
U.S. and Canadian Foods posted a 15 percent rise in operating earnings to $76.8 million.

Quaker said worldwide sales of Gatorade sports drink, its single largest brand, rose 3 percent to $538.9 million. International Gatorade sales were up 19 percent, while sales were virtually flat in the United States due to cooler, wetter spring weather in May.
Total beverage operating income was $93.7 million after a $1.1 million pretax charge, compared with $91.3 million a year ago.
Within the Gatorade franchise, the new Frost line has already topped $100 million in sales, and could post sales of $130 million for the year.
"Frost is performing better than we expected," said James Doyle, Quaker executive vice president who in in charge of the beverage business.
He said Frost, on its own, is already the second-largest sports drink in the category behind Gatorade.
The Snapple business had $75.9 million in sales and $5.6 million in operating losses in the second quarter before its sale on May 22.
Meanwhile, Smithburg said the Quaker board is making progress in its search for his successor. Smithburg said in April he plans to step down after 16 years as chairman and chief executive officer.
Quaker Oats stock was up $2.0625 to $47.1875 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
